title: Sentinel Lattice: primary nav reframe and role-aware quick-jumps
creator: Avery Kim
description: Objective: Reframe the Redwood Console primary navigation to reduce cognitive overhead for multi-tenant orgs, surface rollouts and cost telemetry more directly, and introduce a role-aware quick-jump system for commonly used workflows. Problem: engineers and platform teams spend excessive time hunting for model rollouts, cost breakdowns by route, and workspace contexts when switching between hosted/dedicated/private views. This ticket delivers high-fidelity prototypes, usability learnings, interaction specs, and an implementation handoff for a compact left-rail + quick-jump launcher pattern (Sentinel Lattice).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Left-rail compact mode prototype validated with 6 usability sessions showing >=15% reduction in time-to-open rollout page; 2) Quick-jump launcher supports role-aware suggestions (Engineer, PM, Operator) and persists last-5 routes; 3) Cost lens path available in top-level nav with single-click access to per-route cost breakdown; 4) Interaction spec and aria/accessibility annotations documented; 5) Engineering signoff on render performance for orgs with >100 projects (no perceivable lag); 6) Handoff includes Figma frames, storybook-ready components and acceptance E2E checklist.
design_notes: Pattern: 'Sentinel Lattice' combines a compact left rail with an ephemeral quick-jump (Cmd-K style) that is role-aware and surfaced on hover/focus for power users.
Navigation affordances: Primary items (Dashboard, Models, Rollouts, Cost, Observability, Admin) remain persistent; secondary contextual actions are surfaced via quick-jump to reduce vertical length.
Role-aware suggestions: Uses a simple client-side mapping for first-pass suggestions (Engineer: Rollouts/Logs; PM: Dashboards/Evals; Operator: Capacity/Quota) to avoid backend dependency in MVP.
Cost-first access: Add 'Cost' as a top-level node with two entry points — 'Overview' (org-level) and 'By Route' — to shorten common paths for cost analysis.
Progressive disclosure: For orgs with many workspaces/projects show 'Workspace clusters' (collapsible) with search-as-you-type; default to user's last active workspace.
Trade-offs considered: Compact left-rail reduces discoverability for infrequent users; mitigations include onboarding tooltip and a short animated reveal on first login after rollout.
Accessibility: Ensure keyboard focus order mirrors visual order; quick-jump supports arrow navigation and typeahead with ARIA live regions for suggestion updates.
Performance constraints: Avoid server round-trips on key interactions; cache workspace list and recent routes in local storage with 24h TTL.
Visual spec: 48px touch targets in expanded view, 40px in compact; icon-only compact rail with hover-expansion; color tokens follow console theme tokens (token names attached in Figma frames).
decisions: Chosen pattern: Compact left-rail + ephemeral quick-jump (over a persistent top nav) to preserve vertical space for dashboards and model canvases.
Role-aware mapping will be client-first for MVP; server-driven personalization deferred to a follow-up (PM-14210) where telemetry signals will inform suggestions.
Cost node promoted to top-level to reduce clicks to per-route cost views after internal analytics showed cost queries were the 2nd-most common support topic.
We will not collapse all workspaces into a single list by default; instead we show clusters and allow pinning of 3 high-priority workspaces per user.
Keyboard-first interactions prioritized: quick-jump opens with Cmd/Ctrl-K and supports '/' as an alternative in search-focused contexts.
Rollout quick-action: inline 'open rollout' action available from quick-jump suggestions to reduce context switches during incident playbooks.
Prototype fidelity: deliver two Figma variants (compact rail and floating launcher) and a clickable prototype that demonstrates onboarding flows and the cost lens path.
Telemetry hooks: add minimal events for 'quick-jump-open', 'quick-jump-select', 'pin-workspace', 'navigate-cost-by-route' to measure adoption post-launch.

Engineering (Marco Silva): Implementation OK for MVP but needs guardrails for orgs >1000 workspaces; propose server-side index for search-as-you-type if latency >120ms.
Security (Liam Patel): Confirmed client-side suggestion map is low risk; recommend HSM/KMS review only if we persist user pins in encrypted form server-side.
Design Lead (Olga Rios): Prototype variants clarity good; ask to add microcopy for new onboarding tooltip explaining compact vs expanded rail.

usability_findings: 6 participants: 2 Engineers, 2 PMs, 2 Operators; time-to-open-rollout reduced median from 18s -> 13s with quick-jump.
Cost entry path: single-click to 'By Route' reduced number of clicks from 3 -> 1 in 5 of 6 tasks.
Confusion observed: icon-only compact rail initially ambiguous for 2 of 6; mitigated by hover labels and first-run tooltip.
Participants with >20 workspaces expected groupings; the collapsible cluster pattern received positive ratings for scan-ability.
